records.subject: The current label text is: “This water vessel is made of red clay with a rounded body, narrow neck, and repaired rim. It was donated by a Riverside family and displayed beside other household water containers. A catalogue card gives no maker or date. An earlier draft attributed it to artisan Ilyan and dated it to 1842, but neither claim appears in the provenance register. The vessel may have been used for household water storage, though no record identifies its owner or exact purpose. Similar shapes occur in several neighboring settlements. The label describes visible features and limits of current research; it does not establish where the clay was collected or who formed the vessel. Community reviewers are examining the family history; any new attribution awaits evidence review.” The text is 122 words; case ROOM-5 allows 90.

records.subject: Community protocol CP-86 v2 applies to object OBJ-91, front image IMG-91A, detail image IMG-91B, label L-91, and online preview OP-86. The restriction is scoped to OBJ-91 and its derived images; it does not name OBJ-86.
